column1: # autoconfig group, build A (note 0009 D7.1, B03). Builder A, 2026-11-20.
# Sources: EasyMesh through the usp-spec MCP server (doc easymesh): §3.1.2 Conventions (byte/bit order per [2] =
#   IEEE 1905.1, i.e. multi-octet integers big-endian), §2 References, §17.2.1 Table 23, §17.2.2 Table 24,
#   §17.2.3 Table 25, §17.2.4 Table 26, §17.2.5 Table 27, §17.2.47 Table 69, §17.2.51 Table 73 (Profile-2 Error
#   Code), §17.2.74 Table 96 (BSSID), §17.2.77 Table 99 (Agent List). IEEE 1905.1 (doc ieee1905): §6.4.14
#   (receiver dispatch), :1847 (added to Topology Response). Lenient Profile form: em_configuration.cpp:3614
#   (add_tlv ... sizeof(em_profile_type_t)), receiver em_msg.cpp:131-150 (accepts 1 or 4 octets, reads value[0]).
#   TLV codes checked against the tables and em-types codes.rs:254-258 (0x0d-0x11), 261-265 (0x80-0x84),
#   336-338 (0x10), 339-342 (0x11). 0xf2 has no audit row (upstream's own TLV). Note 0009 D1 (0xf2 in scope),
#   D2 (raw reserved values, zero counts), D3 lines 337/340, D4 (Profile 4-octet lenient form; SSID length counting
#   a NUL is a spec form), D5 (WSC body = attribute list as bytes), D6 rule in D3 (host-order fields little-endian).
# Wire layouts (hex = tlvValue only; EasyMesh/1905.1 multi-octet integers big-endian per EasyMesh §3.1.2):
#   0x80/0x81: [0] k = Num_Service, then k x service(1). k may be 0 (D2; no "one or more"). Values 0x02-0xff (0x80),
#         0x01-0xff (0x81) reserved, carried raw (audit 26 EM+ 0xa0/0xa1). k > 8 is valid (audit 27 SPEC).
#   0x82: [0..6) RUID; exactly 6 (Table 25; audit 31 SPEC).   0xb8: [0..6) BSSID; exactly 6 (Table 96; audit 227).
#   0x83: [0] Num_Radio, then per radio { RUID(6), Num_BSS(1), Num_BSS x { AP_MAC(6), SSID Length n(1), SSID(n) } }.
#         Num_Radio and Num_BSS may be 0 (Table 26 "if Num_BSS = 0, these fields are omitted"; audit 35). The SSID is
#         n raw octets; the table sets no maximum and no terminator. An SSID whose last octet is 0x00 (upstream's
#         strlen+1, audit 33) is a spec case (D4), including 33 octets for a 32-character SSID.
#   0x84: [0] Num_BSS, then per BSS { AP_MAC(6), Num_Client(2, BE), Num_Client x { STA_MAC(6), Assoc_time(2, BE) } }.
#         Num_BSS and Num_Client may be 0. Assoc_time 0xffff ("65,535 or higher") carried raw.
#   0xb3: [0] Multi-AP Profile; exactly 1 (Table 69; audits 164/165 SPEC). 0x00 and 0x04-0xff reserved, carried raw (D2).
#         Lenient (D4): 4 octets = profile octet + 3 octets (upstream LE enum, 0N 00 00 00), normalised to the profile octet.
#   0xbc: [0] Reason_Code, then conditional: BSSID(6) iff reason 0x07/0x08/0x0e; Service Prioritization Rule ID(4, BE)
#         iff 0x01/0x02; QMID(2, BE) iff 0x0b; nothing for any other value (incl. reserved). Table 73; audits 181/182.
#   0xd5: [0] Num_Agent, then Num_Agent x { AL MAC(6), Multi-AP Profile(1), Security(1) } (Table 99; audit 238:
#         length = 1 + 8*Num_Agent). Num_Agent may be 0. Reserved profile/security values carried raw.
#   0x0d/0x0f: [0] role; exactly 1. 0x01-0xff reserved, raw.  0x0e/0x10: [0] band; exactly 1. 0x03 (6 GHz, EasyMesh
#         Table 15 per audit 332/333; reserved per 1905.1 Tables 6-23/6-25, D3 line 337) and 0x04-0xff raw.
#   0x11: n octets = the WSC attribute list, any n including 0 (Table 6-26; D3 line 340, D5). Not walked by the body.
#   0xf2: [0] radios_num, then per radio { ruid(6), bss_num(1), bss_num x { bssid(6), haultype(2, LE), vap_mode(2, LE) } }
#         (em_base.h:1616-1632, packed; upstream writes unsigned short in host order, D6 -> little-endian). Counts may be 0
#         (sender writes get_num_radios() and bss_num starting at 0, em_configuration.cpp:1549-1556). Values raw u16.
#   (1) Fields are listed in wire order. A count item (services, radios, rN_bss, bss, bN_clients, agents) is the count
#       value written on the wire; only the entries listed follow it (a count above the listed entries = overstated).
#       For 0x84, bN_clients is 2 octets BE. For 0x11, `attrs` is the number of attributes and is NOT on the wire.
#   (2) SSIDs (rN_bM_ssid=hex:...) are raw octets; SSID Length = their octet count unless rN_bM_ssid_len is given,
#       which then is the length octet written (overstated length).
#   (3) An item given as hex: where it normally takes a MAC/integer is a cut field: exactly those raw bytes are written.
#       An entry field omitted from the list (e.g. missing assoc time, vap mode, BSSID) is absent from the bytes.
#   (4) `trailing`/`partial`/`pad` are raw bytes appended after the listed fields. `pad` marks the lenient 4-octet
#       Profile form (kind=lenient): the expected decoded value is `profile`; the strict decoder rejects the same bytes.
#   (5) Integers: 0x84 Num_Client and assoc_time are decimal, 2 octets BE; 0xbc rule_id 4 octets BE, qmid 2 octets BE;
#       0xf2 haul_type and vap_mode 2 octets little-endian; all other 0x-hex items are 1 octet.
#   (6) 0x11 WSC: each attribute aN_id/aN_value is written as id(2, BE), length(2, BE) = octet count of aN_value, value.
#       `raw=hex:` gives the whole value as raw bytes.
#   (7) 0xbc: bssid/rule_id/qmid are on the wire iff listed in fields, in table order BSSID, Rule ID, QMID.
# Choices: (a) every cut field, partial entry or overstated count/length is error=Truncated (as B01/B02); extra octets
#   after a complete fixed layout are TrailingBytes. (b) 0xbc: a reserved reason code has no conditional fields, so
#   octets after it are TrailingBytes. (c) 0x11 attr-length-overstates is kind=spec: the body carries bytes; WscAttrIter
#   reports the bad attribute later (D5). (d) 0x83 ssid-33-ends-nul is kind=spec (Table 26 sets no maximum; D4).
#   (e) clients-overstate-be pins BE Num_Client: 0x0100 with one client is Truncated (an LE reader would read 1).
#   (f) 0xb3: the 2-, 3- and 5-octet forms are invalid TrailingBytes (no sender writes them; D4).

# Coordinator correction 2026-11-20: the WSC body (0x11) validates that the value is a well-formed attribute list (walked with WscAttrIter), so attr-length-overstates is kind=invalid, error=Truncated.
# Coordinator correction 2026-11-20: 0xd5 partial-agent declares one agent and carries 7 extra octets, so its error is TrailingBytes (was Truncated); applied to both builds identically.
